item.title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of the Hong Kong Krabby Harvestman (Heterobiantes geniculatus) (Opiliones: Epedanidae)
item.description:
Aidie Chen, Chao Zhang, Desmond Kai Teck Tan, Jonathan J. Fong
Scientific Data
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08644-8
Abstract Harvestmen (order Opiliones) are a diverse order within Arachnida that are widely distributed across the globe, and are known for their ecological roles as detritivores and predators in terrestrial ecosystems. However, the scarcity of high-quality genomic resources, especially for Asian endemic lineages, has hindered research into their morphological adaptations and evolutionary history. Here, we generated a chromosome-level genome assembly for the Hong Kong Krabby Harvestman ( Heterobiantes geniculatus ), a species endemic to Asia belonging to the family Epedanidae (Opiliones: Laniatores), by integrating PacBio HiFi long reads, Illumina short reads, RNA-seq, and Hi-C chromatin conformation capture technologies. The final genome assembly spans 3.15 Gb, with a scaffold N50 of 101.15 Mb, and a contig N50 of 8.10 Mb. Notably, 82.91% of the assembly was anchored onto 25 pseudochromosomes, and BUSCO assessment revealed a high genome completeness of 97.4%, indicating excellent assembly quality. This chromosome-level genome represents the first high-quality genomic resource for the genus Heterobiantes , providing a critical foundation for future investigations into the genetic basis of its specialized phenotypic adaptations, reconstructing the evolutionary history of Epedanidae, and resolving phylogenetic controversies within Opiliones.

item.title: COVID Diaries, U.S. Media Response to COVID Vaccination Program, December 2020 to September 2021
item.description:
Avalon S. Moore, Bridget Vitu, Felicia Fraizer-Bisner, Peter J. Williams, Madeline Chun, Claire Archer, Abdelrhman Gouda, Akhil Vallabh, et al.
Scientific Data
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08697-9
Abstract We present a curated dataset of U.S. news coverage of the COVID-19 vaccination rollout to support research on media communication during a public health emergency. The dataset contains 5,317 unique URLs from 20 nationwide, open-access media outlets, spanning December 2020 (Phase 1a allocation) through September 2021 (broad availability and emerging mandates). Outlets were selected based on a survey of 489 U.S. adults identifying their primary sources of information about the vaccination program. For each publication, we provide outlet, date, headline, original URL, and a permanent link. These records capture the contemporaneous media environment in which individuals sought information and made decisions about COVID-19 vaccination. The dataset enables analyses of topical emphasis, framing, and agenda-setting across outlets and over time, and provides a resource for reproducible research on audience segmentation, economic drivers of content, and editorial retention strategies during the COVID-19 vaccination campaign.

item.title: Dataset of family happiness index among the Hong Kong general population from 2019 to 2025
item.description:
Simon Ching Lam, Aderonke Odetayo, Shun Chan, Kwai-Yu Tsui, Daniel Tan Lei Shek, Ken Hok Man Ho, Daphne Sze Ki Cheung, Summer Cho Ngan Siu, et al.
Scientific Data
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08635-9
Abstract Family happiness is important to society, serving as a social construct in which individual well-being is connected to broader social and economic dynamics. Understanding the multilevel factors associated with family happiness is crucial for effective public mental health and development policies. Several frameworks on happiness have been developed from an individualistic context. However, empirical research on family happiness in changing situations remains sparse. To this end, we present a multiyear dataset collected from 7,744 participants across three distinct situations: the 2019 social unrest, the 2021–2022 coronavirus pandemic, and the 2023–2025 post-pandemic recovery phase. Data was collected using online and/or face-to-face methods. The dataset includes self-reported measurements and demographic information. The dataset’s strength lies in its temporal scope, providing a rare baseline that spans major events in Hong Kong, offering granular insights for the empirical evaluation of happiness models in families, and contributing to local and international policy agendas. Data validation protocols and calculated index mean scores for some variables have been added to optimize data analytical readiness.

item.title: Translatome data of bundle sheath and mesophyll cells of leaves of the C4 species Flaveria bidentis
item.description:
Stefanie Schulze, Peter Westhoff
Scientific Data, vol. 13, issue 1
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08636-8
Abstract C 4 photosynthesis, a specialized form of photosynthesis that uses a CO 2 concentrating mechanism, evolved more than 60 times independently within various families of the angiosperms. This evolution entailed anatomical and biochemical changes within the plants which were accompanied by a plethora of differentially expressed genes. The differentiation of bundle sheath and mesophyll cells in the leaves was an essential anatomical adaption in many C 4 species and was accompanied by a differential distribution of photosynthetic processes between these two cell types, whereas in C 3 species each leaf chlorenchyma cell is able of carrying out all photosynthetic reactions. Leaves of the C 4 Asteracean species Flaveria bidentis were used to generate translatome data for bundle sheath and mesophyll cells allowing to elucidate which genes are expressed differentially between these cell types.
